description: Shares outstanding and cash over time for one company, from its SEC XBRL filings, with the offerings and cash events from its dilution snapshot so each raise can be lined up against the share count and cash around it. Response fields: `sharesOutstanding[]` and `cash[]` (SEC filing data, returned for any company with SEC filings); `fullyDiluted`, `cashEstimate`, `offerings[]` and `cashEvents[]` (from the dilution snapshot, null when the company has not been analysed yet, in which case `offeringMarkers` is "not-covered"); `coverage` (`available`, `unavailableReason`, `status`); and the withheld-row fields. `degraded: true` means an SEC request failed and the series may be incomplete. Each `sharesOutstanding` point is the count as filed, on the split basis in force when it was reported and not rebased to today, so a reverse split shows as a step and a growth rate measured across a split is not meaningful. Each point carries `asOf` (the date the count is stated as of; `periodEnd` is a deprecated alias), `dateKind` ("cover": the cover-page date; "period_end": a balance-sheet date; "stated": a stored count, see below), `filedAt`, `form` (an amendment keeps its "/A"), `accession` and `source`: "sec_xbrl" (the class-less XBRL series), "xbrl_multiclass" (the filing's XBRL instance summed over its common share classes, for issuers that report shares per class), or "stored_count" (the newest count Signal8 holds that the issuer stated as of a date, appended only when newer than every XBRL point and read from a filing not already in the series; it carries that filing's `filedAt`, `form` and `accession`, and `storedSource` names its source). Each filing contributes one point: its cover-page count, or its balance-sheet count when the filing has no cover count. A count Signal8 only confirmed against a market-data figure has no reported date and is not a point. A new 10-Q, 10-K, 20-F or 40-F appears on the next request once SEC's data API lists it, usually within minutes of the filing. A count dated more than about 400 days before its own filing is dropped as a stale recital. `sharesOutstandingCoverage` explains the series: `xbrlReason` is non-null when there is no XBRL point ("sec_unreachable", "no_share_facts_filed", "multiclass_periods_incomplete", "all_facts_before_window" for anything older than `windowStart`, or "all_facts_stale"), and `storedCount` says whether a stored count was appended and if not why. An empty series is not a count of zero. `offerings[]` rows carry `eventDate` (an offering's closing date, else its pricing date, never a filing date; `eventDateKind` says which) and `primarySource` {accession, formType, filingDate, url, sourceKind}, the offering prospectus or current report among the row's citations where one exists (`sourceKind: "later_report"` = only a periodic report cites it). Their `accessionNumber`, `formType` and `filingDate` are deprecated copies of `primarySource`. Offering share counts and prices are on the current split basis; ATM sales and note conversions are as reported. `fullyDiluted` is on the current split basis. A gap in the series means no filing covered that period, not that the count was unchanged. Returns HTTP 200 when the snapshot is unavailable (read `coverage`); 404 only when the ticker maps to no SEC filer. A null, absent or withheld value means the figure was not measured; it does not mean "no dilution", "no warrants", "no shelf" or zero. A numeric 0 is a measured zero, so availability is carried by the availability, withheld and reason fields, not by the value. Included in Signal8 Pro: without it the call returns 403 FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE with `requiredTier: "pro"` (a tier upgrade; there is no add-on to buy).

ticker.description: Company identifier: the current ticker (e.g. "AAPL"), a former ticker of a renamed or delisted company (e.g. "MIGI", now BGDE), or a numeric SEC CIK (e.g. "320193" or "0000320193"). A former ticker or a CIK is answered with a `resolvedFrom` block naming the current symbol.
